## Standards reference

**Express.js backend**

- Feature-folder architecture; one folder per domain under `src/features/<domain>/` containing `<domain>.routes.ts`, `<domain>.controller.ts`, `<domain>.service.ts`, `<domain>.repository.ts`, `<domain>.schema.ts`; shared middleware and types in `src/shared/`
- Request validation with **Zod** on every request body, query param, and path param
- JWT authentication middleware (`src/shared/middleware/auth.middleware.ts`)
- RBAC with roles: `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, `guest`
- Centralised error handler middleware for uniform error responses
- Prisma as the ORM; schema-first DB design
- REST API: `GET /api/v1/resources`, `POST /api/v1/resources`, etc.
- Response envelope: `{ data, meta }` for success; `{ error, details }` for errors
- Rate limiting with `express-rate-limit` (1000 req/hour authenticated, 100 req/hour anonymous)
- Enable `helmet()` globally for security headers
- Enable `cors()` with strict origin whitelist from env

**React frontend**

- Vite + React + TypeScript strict mode; functional components only; no class components
- PascalCase component names; kebab-case file names
- Tailwind CSS for all styling; no inline styles
- TanStack Query v5 for all server state; Axios for HTTP calls
- Zustand for global client state
- React Router v6 for routing
- Error boundaries at page and layout level
- Prettier + ESLint enforced

**Testing**

- **Jest** for backend unit tests (services, repositories) — mocked IO, no network or filesystem
- **Jest + React Testing Library** for frontend component tests — mocked Axios
- **Playwright** for E2E tests — runs against a local dev stack
- TDD: read test contracts from PLAN.md → create stubs → implement → make tests pass
- Minimum ≥80% coverage on all new/changed code

**Security (OWASP Top 10)**

- Input validation and output encoding at all boundaries (Zod schemas)
- Secrets in environment variables only — never hardcoded
- Passwords hashed with bcryptjs (min cost factor 12)
- JWT HS256; 1-hour access token expiry + 7-day refresh token
- Sensitive fields never logged (passwords, tokens, PII)

Before entering Phase 1, read the following files. Stop and report any that are missing.

2. `<output_dir>/DESIGN.md` — screens, components, tokens, Figma node IDs.
3. `<output_dir>/DB_SCHEMA.md` — authoritative schema; drives Prisma models.

## Phase 1 — Setup frontend & backend

**TODO checklist (print at phase start):**

- [ ] Read and summarise PLAN.md / ARCHITECTURE.md
- [ ] Initialise backend project with `npm init`
- [ ] Initialise frontend project with Vite CLI
- [ ] Configure TypeScript (strict mode) for both projects
- [ ] Set up ESLint + Prettier for both projects
- [ ] Verify both projects start without errors (`npm run dev`)

### 1.1 — Read outputs and plan

Read all pre-flight files. Build an internal summary of every domain, endpoint, and screen. Do not write any application code yet.

### 1.2 — Bootstrap backend

Inside `generated/<project-name>/backend/`, always use the **official CLI or init tool for the chosen stack**. `npm init` is the example for Node.js/Express — it is not a universal default. Rules:

- **Express.js:** `npm init -y` then install Express manually (see runtime deps in Phase 3).
- **NestJS:** `nest new backend`
- **Fastify:** `fastify generate backend`
- **Any other stack:** research its official scaffolding CLI and use it. Never fall back to bare `npm init` for a framework that ships its own CLI.

Create the **feature-folder** skeleton — directories only, no application code:

```
backend/
├── src/
│   ├── features/         # one sub-folder per domain (auth, users, products, …)
│   ├── middleware/
│   ├── types/
│   ├── app.ts
│   └── server.ts
├── prisma/
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   └── integration/
├── tsconfig.json
└── package.json
```

Configure `tsconfig.json` with `"strict": true`.
Add scripts to `package.json`: `"build"`, `"dev"`, `"lint"`, `"test"`.

### 1.3 — Bootstrap frontend

Inside `generated/<project-name>/frontend/`, always use the **official CLI or init tool for the chosen stack**. Vite is the example for React — it is not a universal default. Rules:

- **React + Vite (default):** `npm create vite@latest . -- --template react-ts`
- **Next.js:** `npx create-next-app@latest . --typescript`
- **SvelteKit:** `npx sv create .`
- **Vue + Vite:** `npm create vite@latest . -- --template vue-ts`
- **Any other stack:** research its official scaffolding CLI and use it. Never use the Vite CLI for a framework that ships its own.

Create the **feature-folder** skeleton — directories only:

```
frontend/
├── src/
│   ├── features/         # one sub-folder per feature
│   ├── components/
│   ├── hooks/
│   ├── lib/
│   ├── types/
│   ├── styles/
│   └── main.tsx
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   └── e2e/
├── tsconfig.json
└── package.json
```

### 1.4 — Verify phase completion

Run `npm run dev` (or equivalent) for both projects and confirm they start without errors.

**✅ Phase 1 gate:** Re-print the TODO checklist. All items must be ✅ before proceeding to Phase 2.

## Phase 2 — Install, setup Prisma & create the DB schema

**TODO checklist (print at phase start):**

- [ ] Install Prisma CLI and `@prisma/client` via npm
- [ ] Initialise Prisma (`npx prisma init`)
- [ ] Write `prisma/schema.prisma` from `DB_SCHEMA.md`
- [ ] Run initial migration (`npx prisma migrate dev --name init`)
- [ ] Verify migration output matches `DB_SCHEMA.md` Migration Order
- [ ] Generate Prisma client (`npx prisma generate`)

### 2.1 — Install Prisma

Inside `backend/`:

```bash
npm install @prisma/client
npm install --save-dev prisma
```

### 2.2 — Initialise Prisma

```bash
npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite
```

For production targets, swap to `postgresql` and configure `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`.

### 2.3 — Write the schema

Create `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` based on `DB_SCHEMA.md`:

- One `model` per entity; follow DB_SCHEMA.md naming exactly.
- Proper relations with referential actions (`onDelete`, `onUpdate`).
- `@unique` constraints and `@@index` declarations as specified.
- `createdAt DateTime @default(now())` and `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` on every model.
- Soft-delete pattern (`deletedAt DateTime?`) where DB_SCHEMA.md specifies it.

### 2.4 — Run migration and generate client

```bash
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
npx prisma generate
```

Verify the generated migration SQL matches the Migration Order in `DB_SCHEMA.md`.

**✅ Phase 2 gate:** Re-print the TODO checklist. All items must be ✅ before proceeding to Phase 3.

## Phase 3 — Create the backend service

**TODO checklist (print at phase start):**

- [ ] Install all runtime and dev dependencies
- [ ] Write Jest test stubs for every domain (TDD)
- [ ] Write required mocks (Prisma, external services)
- [ ] Implement all routes, controllers, services, repositories, Zod schemas
- [ ] Implement authentication (register / login / refresh / logout) and JWT/RBAC middleware
- [ ] Apply security hardening (helmet, cors, rate-limit, error handler)
- [ ] Run tests → fix all failures → reach ≥80% coverage
- [ ] Run build → fix all TypeScript / lint errors

### 3.1 — Install dependencies

Runtime:

```bash
npm install express @prisma/client zod jsonwebtoken bcryptjs helmet cors express-rate-limit dotenv
```

Dev:

```bash
npm install --save-dev typescript ts-node-dev @types/express @types/node @types/jsonwebtoken @types/bcryptjs jest ts-jest @types/jest supertest @types/supertest eslint prettier
```

For non-Express stacks, install the equivalent packages for that framework.

### 3.2 — Write test stubs (TDD — write tests before implementation)

For every domain in `API_SPEC.md`, create **empty stub files** (`describe` / `it` blocks with no bodies):

- `backend/tests/unit/<domain>.service.test.ts` — service business logic
- `backend/tests/integration/<domain>.controller.test.ts` — controller request/response shapes

Create shared mocks:

- `backend/tests/__mocks__/prisma.ts` — mock `PrismaClient` using `jest.mock`
- Mock any external services (email, payment, storage) with `jest.fn()` factories

Do **not** implement test bodies yet. Confirm all stub files exist before moving to 3.3.

### 3.3 — Implement all routes

For each domain in `API_SPEC.md`, implement in this order: **Zod schema → Repository → Service → Controller → Router**.

Feature-folder layout per domain:

```
src/features/<domain>/
├── <domain>.schema.ts       # Zod request/response schemas
├── <domain>.repository.ts   # Prisma queries only
├── <domain>.service.ts      # Business logic; calls repository
├── <domain>.controller.ts   # Request/response handling; calls service
└── <domain>.routes.ts       # Express router; mounts controller handlers
```

Shared:

```
src/shared/middleware/
├── auth.middleware.ts        # Verify JWT; attach user to req
├── validate.middleware.ts    # Generic Zod validation middleware
└── error.middleware.ts       # Centralised error handler
src/shared/types/index.ts     # Shared TypeScript types
src/app.ts                    # Express app factory (mounts routers, middleware)
src/server.ts                 # Entry point (starts HTTP server)
```

### 3.4 — Implement authentication

- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` — hash password with bcryptjs (cost ≥12), create user, issue tokens
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` — verify credentials, issue access token (1 h) + refresh token (7 d)
- `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` — validate refresh token, issue new access token
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` — invalidate refresh token
- JWT middleware: verify `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; reject with 401 on failure
- RBAC middleware: enforce per-route role requirements (`admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, `guest`)

### 3.5 — Security hardening

- `helmet()` and `cors()` (strict origin whitelist from env) applied globally in `app.ts`
- `express-rate-limit`: 1 000 req/h authenticated, 100 req/h anonymous
- Every request body, query param, and path param validated via `validate.middleware.ts` + Zod
- Centralised error handler: never leak stack traces; always return `{ error, details }` envelope
- Secrets in `.env` only; never hardcoded; sensitive fields never logged

### 3.6 — Implement tests

Fill in the stub files from 3.2:

- **Unit tests:** mock Prisma via `__mocks__/prisma.ts`; test service logic in isolation
- **Integration tests:** mock the service layer; test controller input validation and response envelopes
- Run `npx jest --coverage` and iterate until **all tests pass** and **coverage ≥80%** on all changed files

### 3.7 — Verification loop

Repeat until all checks pass:

```
LOOP:
  1. npm run build           — fix TypeScript compilation errors
  2. npm run lint            — fix ESLint errors
  3. npx jest --coverage     — fix failing tests; improve coverage if <80%
  4. Security audit:
       a. No hardcoded secrets
       b. All protected endpoints have auth middleware
       c. All request bodies validated with Zod
       d. Error responses never leak stack traces
  5. Verify every endpoint in API_SPEC.md is implemented
  6. Any failure → fix and restart loop
  7. All pass → backend VERIFIED ✅
```

**✅ Phase 3 gate:** Re-print the TODO checklist. All items must be ✅ before proceeding to Phase 4.

### 4.2 — Configure theme

### 4.3 — Fetch Figma design context

For each screen listed in PLAN.md Phase 5:

1. Call `get_design_context` with the screen's Figma node ID.
2. Call `get_screenshot` to capture the visual reference.

### 4.4 — Write test stubs (TDD — write tests before implementation)

Create **empty stub files** before writing any component code:

- `frontend/tests/e2e/<flow>.spec.ts` — Playwright stubs

Create shared mocks:

- `frontend/src/__mocks__/axios.ts` — mock Axios with `jest.mock`

### 4.5 — Build shared components

Build in this order; do not start feature components until shared components are done:

1. **Atoms** — Button, Input, Badge, Icon, Spinner, …
2. **Molecules** — FormField, Card, NavItem, Toast, …
3. **Organisms** — Header, Sidebar, DataTable, Modal, …

All components: PascalCase name; kebab-case file name; no `any` types; no inline styles; Figma comment at top.

### 4.5a — Apply motion & animation (follow `ui-animation` skill)

After building all shared components and before starting feature pages, add motion following the rules in the [ui-animation skill](../../.agents/skills/ui-animation/SKILL.md). Every element that appears, disappears, or responds to user interaction **must** have intentional motion.

**Mandatory animation targets:**

| Element | Animation type | Implementation |
|---------|---------------|----------------|
| Page transitions | Fade + translate-Y (subtle) | `framer-motion` `AnimatePresence` + `motion.div` |
| Modal / drawer open/close | Scale from origin + fade | `framer-motion` with `initial`, `animate`, `exit` |
| Button press / hover | Scale down (0.97) on press; subtle brightness lift on hover | CSS `active:scale-97` + `transition` or `motion.button` |
| Form field focus | Border colour transition + label float | CSS `transition-colors` |
| Toast / notification entry | Slide in from edge + fade | `framer-motion` `AnimatePresence` |
| List item appearance | Staggered fade + translate-Y | `motion.li` with `staggerChildren` |
| Loading skeleton | Shimmer sweep | CSS `@keyframes` or Tailwind `animate-pulse` |
| Card hover | Subtle lift (shadow + translate-Y: -2px) | CSS `transition-shadow transition-transform` |
| Navigation active indicator | Smooth slide between items | `framer-motion` layout animation |
| Dropdown / popover | Scale from anchor + fade | `framer-motion` |

**Rules (from `ui-animation` skill):**
- Use `framer-motion` for all JavaScript-driven animations; use CSS transitions for simple hover/focus states.
- All durations 150 ms – 400 ms. Nothing slower without strong justification.
- Use spring physics (`type: "spring"`) for interactive/gesture animations; use `ease` curves for entry/exit.
- Never animate `width` or `height` directly — use `scaleX`/`scaleY` or `framer-motion` layout animations.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: wrap all `motion` components with the `useReducedMotion` hook and fall back to instant transitions.
- Do **not** add animation for animation's sake — every motion must communicate state or guide attention.

### 4.6 — Build feature components and pages

Complete **one feature end-to-end** before starting the next (components → hooks → page → route):

- Components in `src/features/<feature>/components/`
- TanStack Query hooks in `src/features/<feature>/hooks/`
- Pages in `src/features/<feature>/pages/`
- Zustand slices in `src/features/<feature>/store/` (if needed)

For each page:

1. Add the route to `src/router.tsx`.
2. Wire up TanStack Query hooks for all data fetching and mutations.
3. Implement loading, error, and empty states for every async operation.
4. Add an error boundary at the page level.

### 4.7 — Axios client & TanStack Query setup

`src/shared/lib/api-client.ts`:

- Base URL from `VITE_API_URL` env var
- Request interceptor: attach `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- Response interceptor: on 401, attempt token refresh; on persistent failure, redirect to `/login`
- Never log request/response bodies containing credentials

`src/shared/lib/query-client.ts`:

- Configure stale times and cache times per resource type
- `QueryClientProvider` in `src/main.tsx`

### 4.8 — Authentication flow

- Login and register pages: `src/features/auth/pages/`
- Zustand auth store: `src/features/auth/store/auth.store.ts`
  - Access token in memory (Zustand); refresh token in httpOnly cookie
- `<ProtectedRoute>` wrapper: `src/features/auth/components/protected-route.tsx`

### 4.9 — Implement tests

Fill in the stub files from 4.4:

- **Unit/component tests:** mock Axios; assert rendering, user interactions, and data states (loading / error / empty / populated)
- **Playwright E2E tests:** test full user flows against the local dev stack
- Run `npx jest --coverage` and `npx playwright test`, iterating until **all tests pass** and **unit coverage ≥80%**

### 4.10 — Animation review (follow `review-animations` skill)

Before marking Phase 4 complete, run a full animation review following the [review-animations skill](../../.agents/skills/review-animations/SKILL.md).

For **every** animated element in the codebase:

1. Check against the craft bar defined in the skill — default is to **flag**; approval is earned.
2. Fix all flagged issues before proceeding.
3. Verify `prefers-reduced-motion` fallbacks are present on every `motion.*` component.
4. Confirm no animation uses `width`, `height`, or `margin` as animated properties.
5. Confirm all spring configs have `damping` and `stiffness` explicitly set (no defaults).

### 4.11 — Verification loop

Repeat until all checks pass:

```
LOOP:
  1. npm run build              — fix TypeScript and Vite build errors
  2. npm run lint               — fix ESLint / Prettier errors
  3. npx jest --coverage        — fix failing tests; improve coverage if <80%
  4. npx playwright test        — fix failing E2E tests
  5. For each screen:
       a. Compare page against the Figma screenshot
       b. Verify all interactive elements (forms, buttons, nav) work
       c. Verify data-fetch states (loading, error, empty, populated)
       d. Verify responsive behaviour at sm / md / lg / xl
       e. Verify all animated elements feel intentional and smooth
       f. Verify prefers-reduced-motion is respected (test in browser DevTools)
  6. Any defect → fix, restart loop
  7. All screens pass → frontend VERIFIED ✅
```

## Phase 5 — Generate seed data

**TODO checklist (print at phase start):**

- [ ] Create `backend/prisma/seed.ts`
- [ ] Cover every entity with at least one seed record
- [ ] Include seed users for every role (like `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, etc - whichever are defined in DB_SCHEMA.md)
- [ ] Hash all seed passwords & any sensivtive data like `api_key` etc with bcryptjs
- [ ] Wrap seed in a transaction; use `upsert` for idempotency
- [ ] Add `"db:seed"` script to `backend/package.json`
- [ ] Run `npm run db:seed` and verify all records are created without errors
- [ ] Spot-check sample data for realism and correctness

### 5.1 — Create seed.ts

Create `backend/prisma/seed.ts`:

1. Follow the **Seed Data Requirements** section of `DB_SCHEMA.md` for record counts and example values.
2. Create at least one record per entity.
3. Create seed users for every role: `admin`, `editor`, `viewer` (and any domain-specific roles).
4. Hash all passwords with `bcryptjs` (cost factor ≥12).
5. Wrap all inserts in a Prisma `$transaction`; use `upsert` to make the script safely re-runnable.

### 5.2 — Register and run the script

Add to `backend/package.json`:

```json
"db:seed": "ts-node prisma/seed.ts"
```

Run: `npm run db:seed`

Verify output: every entity table must contain the expected number of records. Fix any errors and re-run until clean.

### 5.3 — Spot-check data

Query the SQLite database (or use `npx prisma studio`) to confirm:

- All expected tables are populated.
- Relations (foreign keys) resolve correctly.
- Seed passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes (not plaintext).

**✅ Phase 5 gate:** Re-print the TODO checklist. All items must be ✅ before proceeding to Phase 6.

## Phase 6 — Containerisation

**TODO checklist (print at phase start):**

- [ ] Create `infra/` directory
- [ ] Write `infra/Dockerfile.backend`
- [ ] Write `infra/Dockerfile.frontend`
- [ ] Write `infra/docker-compose.yml` covering all services (FE + BE + any external services)
- [ ] Add `.dockerignore` files to backend and frontend
- [ ] Build each image individually and fix any errors
- [ ] Run `docker compose up` and verify all services start and communicate correctly

### 6.1 — Create infra directory

```
generated/<project-name>/infra/
├── Dockerfile.backend
├── Dockerfile.frontend
└── docker-compose.yml
```

### 6.2 — Backend Dockerfile

`infra/Dockerfile.backend`:

```dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY backend/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY backend/ .
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS production
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/prisma ./prisma
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
```

Add `backend/.dockerignore`: `node_modules`, `dist`, `.env`, `*.test.ts`, `tests/`

### 6.3 — Frontend Dockerfile

`infra/Dockerfile.frontend`:

```dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY frontend/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY frontend/ .
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM nginx:alpine AS production
COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY infra/nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
EXPOSE 80
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
```

Create `infra/nginx.conf` with a basic SPA config (try_files fallback to `index.html`).

Add `frontend/.dockerignore`: `node_modules`, `dist`, `.env`

### 6.4 — Docker Compose

`infra/docker-compose.yml` must include **all** services:

- **frontend** — built from `Dockerfile.frontend`; port 80
- **backend** — built from `Dockerfile.backend`; port 3000; depends on any DB or queue services
- **Any external services** from ARCHITECTURE.md (e.g. PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ) — use official images

Example skeleton (expand as needed for the actual stack):

```yaml
version: "3.9"
services:
  backend:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/Dockerfile.backend
    env_file: ../backend/.env
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    depends_on:
      - db          # include only if using an external DB container

  frontend:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/Dockerfile.frontend
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    depends_on:
      - backend

  # Add db, redis, queue services here if required by ARCHITECTURE.md
```

All secrets and environment variables must come from `.env` files or Docker secrets — never hardcoded.

### 6.5 — Build and smoke-test

1. Build each image individually and fix any errors:
   ```bash
   docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.backend -t <project>-backend ..
   docker build -f infra/Dockerfile.frontend -t <project>-frontend ..
   ```
2. Bring up all services: `docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up --build`
3. Verify:
   - Backend health endpoint responds (e.g. `GET /api/v1/health → 200`)
   - Frontend loads in browser on port 80
   - Backend can reach the database / any external services

**✅ Phase 6 gate:** Re-print the TODO checklist. All items must be ✅. All services running → project COMPLETE ✅.

## Retry policy

- Up to **3 fix passes** per failing check or screen defect within a phase.
- If still unresolved after 3 passes, stop and report:
  - The exact failure
  - All attempted fixes
  - What is blocked and why
  - Which phase is blocked
